 Judgment
The petitioner filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
2. That on 25-08-2019 at about 2-00 p.m. the petitioner was riding his motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-11-L-5624 on extreme left side of the Maddur - Malavalli main road, when he reached near Kullappa Military Hotel, Bugathagahalli Village,
Malavalli Taluk, Mandya Dist., stopped his vehicle on the left side of the road by seeing his villagers and talking with them, at that time, rider of Pulsar motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-02-JR-6295 rode the same in a rash and negligent manner came from Malavalli at high speed and dashed the right side of the petitioner's motor cycle from behind and caused the accident.
Due to the forced impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is further stated that, immediately the petitioner was shifted to Malavalli Government Hospital, wherein he took the first aid treatment, then he was referred to JSS Hospital, M.G.Road, Mysore wherein he was treated as an inpatient and undergone surgery and had spent Rs.2,00,000/-
towards medicines, attendant charges, food and nourishment etc.
4.

It is also stated in the petition that, prior to the accident the petitioner was hale and healthy,
doing agriculture and milk vending and was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month and he used to spend the said amount for the maintenance of her family members.
After the accident, he could not do any work due to his severe injuries.
5. It is alleged in the petition that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Pulsar Motor cycle bearing registration No.KA- 02-JR-6295.
Hence, Malavalli Rural Police have registered criminal case against rider of the offending vehicle in Crime No.116/2019 under section 279 and 338 of IPC.
As such, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition, seeking compensation.
6. In response to the notices, the respondent No.1 has not appeared before the court, remained absent, hence, placed exparte.
On the other hand, respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.

In the written statement of the respondent No.2 stated that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case.

Further, contended that, the alleged accident took place due to the negligent riding of the petitioner by riding his vehicle bearing No.KA-11-L-5624 and not on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA- 01-JR-6295.

It is also contention of the respondent No.2 that the rider of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence to ride the said vehicle and after due investigation jurisdictional police have filed the charge sheet against the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-02-JR-6295 for the offences punishable under section 279, 338 of IPC and Section 3(1) R/W section 181 of IMV Act.
It is also contention of the respondent No.2 that,
as on the date of the accident the petitioner was not wearing helmet with ISI Mark
. Further denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner and expenses incurred towards medical and other incidental charges.

Further contended that the claim of the petitioner is highly excessive,
exaggerated and arbitrary.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.

8. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this court has framed the following issues;
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that, he had sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident,
that was taken place on 25-08-2019 at about 2-00 p.m. on Maddur - Malavalli Main road, near Kullappa Military Hotel, Bugathagahalli village, Malavalli Taluk,
Mandya due to the rash and negligent driving of the rider of the Pulsar Motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-02-JR-6295 in an actionable negligence?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what rate?

from whom?
3) What order or award?
9. In order to substantiate his case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P11.

In addition to his evidence placed the evidence of Dr.Rajesh M.B. as PW2 and got marked the documents as Ex.P12 & Ex.P13.
10.
In order to disprove the contention of the petitioner, the respondent No.2 has examined its Legal Manager as RW1 and got marked the documents as Ex.R1 and Ex.R2.
On the other hand, the respondent No.1 has placed exparte.

11. Heard the arguments of both the counsel and perused the materials available on record.
12.

My answer to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.

13.

It is the specific case of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the Pulsar motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-02-JR-6295,
the alleged accident had taken place, consequently he had sustained grievous injuries.

14. On the other hand, the respondent No.2 being the insurance company, though not disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner, seriously disputed the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the Pulsar motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-02-JR-6295 and also rider of the pulsar motor cycle had no valid and effective driving licence.

In the light of the rival contentions of both the parties,
on going through the above issue burden is on the petitioner to prove the above issue on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities.
15. The petitioner in order to prove his case, examined himself as PW1.
He has reiterated the averments made in the petition.

16. On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that based upon the first information statement given by Kalalingaiah, the S.H.O. of Malavalli Rural Police has registered the case against the rider of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 337 of I.P.C.

Upon investigation, the Investigation Officer of the case has filed charge sheet against the rider of the offending vehicle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 338 of IPC and Section 3 R/W Section 181 of IMV Act.

17. The respondent No.2, disputed the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-02-JR-6295, but not examined the rider of the offending vehicle or any of the independent witness who witnessed the alleged accident to prove the same.

Though the respondent No.2 examined Assistant Manager Legal(Claims) as RW1, but his evidence is only with regard to the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-02-JR-6295 had no valid and effective driving licence to ride the said vehicle as on the date of accident.

18. Though the PW1 was subjected to cross- examine at length, nothing has been elicited from the Dasaratha.S vs Naveen.O on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84315759/
4 mouth of the PW1 that this accident is not due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.

19. In the light of the oral evidence of the PW1 coupled with the police documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P8,
it is clear that the petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident which is result of rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Pulsar motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-02-JR-6295.
Hence, issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2 :
20.
This issue is with respect to the entitlement of reliefs claimed by the petitioner.
The petitioner through this petition, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident under different heads.

21. Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by her,
in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injury cases in Motor Vehicle Act.

Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
"In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.

entities.text: Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency.
The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."

"while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.
That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation."

Pain and Sufferings;
22.
PW1 has stated in his evidence that, he has sustained the injuries in a road traffic accident.
In connection with the injuries he has produced wound certificate marked as Ex.P6.

The said document discloses that, he had sustained the following injuries:-
1. Lacerated wound over right ankle, left side 10x1x1/2 cm fresh bleeding seen.
2. Lacerated wound over right ankle, right side 12x1x1/2 cm fresh bleeding seen.
3. Upper part of right heel seperated from lower part of right heel.

2. CT Scan reveals; Comminuted displaced multifragmentary fracture of right calceneum with intra articular extension at Talocalcaneal joint.
MSCT Head: EDH in frontal convexity, haemorhagic contussion left temporal lobe and fractue of right parietal bone with extention into frontal bone.
23. The doctor is of the opinion that the said injuries are grievous in nature.
Further, the petitioner has produced discharge summary as per Ex.P9 issued by JSS Hospital, Mysore.
On going through the discharge summary reveals that, petitioner was admitted from 25.8.2019 to 14.9.2019.

By taking into consideration of the nature of the injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, he could have undergone pain and sufferings while taking treatment, as an in patient as well as an outpatient.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.
Loss of income during treatment period:
24. PW1 has stated that, he was doing agriculture and milk vending and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
In this regard, he has not placed any document to prove his actual income.

On going through the discharge summary reveals that,
petitioner was admitted from 25.8.2019 to 14.9.2019.

During the period of treatment,
definitely, there was some difficulty to his to do daily routine work and to do his work for livelihood at least for a period of two months by looking in to the nature of the injuries sustained by him.
Hence, I am of the view that, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.28,000/- towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period.

Medical Expeneses;
25.
The petitioner in connection with his treatment expenses produced medical bills at Ex.P13 for Rs.1,77,504/-.
At the time of cross-examination except the suggestion that the medical bills are created, nothing has been placed on record to prove that the medical bills are created for the purpose of this case.

On going through the medical bills Sl.No.1, 12, 13, 14, 21 are advance receipts of Rs.3,000/-, Rs.10,000/-,
Rs.2,000/-, Rs.3,500/- and Rs.16,000/- respectively, in total Rs.34,500/-.
After deducting the said amount it comes to Rs.1,43,004/-.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,43,004/- towards medical expenses.

Attendant charges, food and nourishment and conveyance charges;
26.
The petitioner produced discharge sumnmary issued by JSS hospital, which is marked as Ex.P9.
As per said document the petitoiner took treatment as an inpatient in the said hospital from 25.08.2019 to 14.09.2019 i.e., for about 21 days.
So, definitely the petitioner could have spent some amount towards, food, nourishment, conveyance, as well as towards attendant charges.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.25,000/- towards attendant charges, food,

6 nourishment and conveyance charges.

Loss of future income;
27.
The petitioner herein, asserting that, he had sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injuries sustained by him.
In order to prove the same, the petitioner has relied on his evidence along with the wound certificate and other medical documents.

In the evidence of the PW1,
reiterated the same thing forthcoming in the main petition.
As already discussed above, wound certificate placed by him as per Ex.P6 goes to show that, he had sustained grievous injury for which he took the treatment as an inpatient.
To substantiate this, the petitioner had placed wound certificate for consideration.

Apart from this, another material witness by name Dr.Rajesh M.B.
examined as PW2.
PW2 has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained open type -3B fracture right calcaneum with heel pad injury.
For which the petitioner underwent wound debridement & ORIF with K-wires on 26.8.2019 and wound debridement and SSG right foot on 6.9.2019.
Further, PW2 has stated that, at the time of his examination of the petitioner on 9.1.2024 for assessment of disability, the petitioner has suffered 26% permanent disability of right lower limb.
28. At the time of cross-examination of PW2, stated that he is the treated doctor and admitted that fracture is united.
Further denied the suggestion that petitioner has sustained only simple injuries and he assessed the disability of the petitioner on higher side.
29. Over all appreciation of evidence of PW2 along with the entire medical documents the whole body disability expressed by PW2 as 26% disability for the right lower limb.

Hence, by taking into consideration of point of disability expressed by PW2, it is apt to take whole body disability as 9%
instead of 26%.
The same will meets the ends of justice.
30. In connection with the age of the petitioner is concerned, on going through the cause title of the petition reveals that, as on the date of the petition, his age was 45 years.

In support of the age proof,
he has not placed any document for consideration.
On going through the xerox copy of the Aadhar card, the date of birth of the petitioner has been mentioned as 18.6.1971.
The accident occurred on 25.8.2019.
Therefore, as on the date of accident, the age of the petitioner is considered as 48 years.

To the said age as per Sarla Verma case, multiplier '13' is to be taken into consideration.
31.

Next factual aspect of the income of the petitioner is concerned, in his evidence the petitioner has stated that, prior to the accident he was was doing agriculture and milk vending and getting an income of Rs.20,000/-.
In this regard, there is no iota of documents to show his income per month.
In the absence of the material documents, notional income has to be taken into consideration.
But the said notional income is to be taken judiciously, by taking into consideration of the year of the accident.
It is pertinent to note that, in the case on hand, the alleged accident had taken place in the year 2019.
As per the notional income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the petitioner as Rs.14,000/- for the year 2019.

7 32.

In the light of my detailed discussions held above, no doubt injuries sustained by the petitioner,
definitely come in the way of his future, in a slight manner, to do his daily routine work, as well as to do his work for livelihood on going through his age criteria.

Hence, the petitioner herein, is entitled for compensation under loss of future income as follows:
Rs.14,000 X 12 X 13 X 9/100= Rs.1,96,560/-.
Loss of amenities;
33.

PW1 has stated in his evidence that due to the accidental injuries he cannot walk, stand, sit,
squat on the floor, cannot lift or carry weight, cannot ride vehicle.
On perusal of evidence of PW2 and also medical documents, I am of the view that, the petitioner will suffer a slight problem in future also, to do his normal work, as well as his work for livelihood.
Hence, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities.

34. In connection with the future medication, PW2 has stated in his evidence that, the petitioner needs neurosurgery evaluation for disability assessment of the right hemiparesis as sequel of head injury.
But he has not produced any estimation.
On perusal of evidence of PW2 and also medical documents, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head of future medical expenses.

35. In view of my discussions held above, on various aspects the petitioner is entitled for compensation in to to, under the following heads:
 Compensation heads Compensation  amount  1.Pain and Suffering Rs. 50,000-00 2.Loss of income during Rs. 28,000-00 laid-up period and rest period 3.
Medical expenses Rs.1,43,004-00 4. Attendant, Nourishment Rs. 25,000-00 and Conveyance Charges 5. Loss of future income Rs.1,96,560-00 due to disability 6. Loss of Amenities Rs. 20,000-00 7.
Future medication Rs. 30,000-00 Total Rs.4,92,564-00 36.

Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,92,564/- (Rupees four lakh ninety two thousand five hundred and sixty four only), along with interest @ 6% per annum, as per the preposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in, MFA No.103557/2016,

sentences.text:
LIABILITY:
37.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, due to actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the Pulsar motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-02-JR-6295 alleged accident had taken place.
As such, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
38. The respondent No.2 has contended that the rider of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
Thereby violated the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
As such, insurance company is not liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
To substantiate the same, respondent No.2 has examined Manager-Legal Claim as RW1.
He has reiterated the contents as averred in the written statement.

He has placed policy copy and notice issued to the owner of the offending vehicle as per Ex.R1 & Ex.R2.
39.

In this regard, on going through the charge sheet submitted by the investigation officer, relevant provision has been inserted stating that, at the time of accident the rider of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving license.

To disprove the contents of the charge sheet and to show that,
the rider had valid D.L. no supportive evidence is available on record to impeach the recitals of Ex.P8.
Moreover, respondent No.1 being the owner and the rider of the motor cycle remained absent, placed exparte.
Hence, it is crystal clear that, there is a clear violation of the terms and conditions of the policy.
40. During the course of argument the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has argued that as on the date of accident the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid licence.
It is violation of terms and conditions of the insurance policy.

Hence, respondent No.1 is not liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and has relied the judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.6154/2019 between Hemalatha @ Hema @ Hemavathi & Others Vs. Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd., & Another and MFA 3297/2019 between Adilakshmamma & Others Vs.
Shri Raju B. & Another 41.

1). 2004 (3) SCC 297 between National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Swaran Singh & Others

sentences.text: In the aforesaid case, with due discussions the Hon'ble Apex Court came to the conclusion that, the insurer has satisfactorily proved its defence in accordance with the provision of Section 149(2) R/W Subsection 7, as interpreted by the court.
And the Tribunal can direct the insurer liable to be reimbursed by the insured for the compensation amount, which has been compared to pay to the third party under the award of the Tribunal.
In one word it is necessary to note that, through this authority, highlighted about the concept pay and recovery.

sentences.text: In the aforesaid case it was observed that, where on adjudication of claim under the Act, the Tribunal arise at a conclusion that, the insurer has satisfactorily proved its defence in accordance with law with the provision of Section 149(2) R/W Sub-section 7, the Tribunal can direct that, the insurer is liable to be reimbursed by the insured for the compensation and other amount which it has been compelled to pay to the third party under the award of the Tribunal.
In the aforesaid case also, highlighted about the principle of pay and recovery.

42. On going through the supra decisions, it is to be noted that to protect the interest of third party,
the principle of pay and recovery is applied.

Apart from this, as per the assertion of the petitioner,
insurance policy was valid from 24.7.2019 to 23.7.2020.
The accident had occurred on 25.8.2019.

The said fact has not been denied by the respondent company by placing the insurance policy as per Ex.R1.
43.

In the light of the discussion held above, I am of the view that, though the respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle, cannot escape from his liability to pay compensation to the petitioner, in view of violation of terms and conditions of the policy.

But, to protect the interest of the petitioner, it is necessary to direct the respondent No.2-insurance company to pay compensation to the petitioner and thereafter to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle, through due process of law.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
44.

In view of above discussions on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for  compensation of Rs.4,92,564/- (Rupees  four lakh ninety two thousand five hundred and sixty four only) along with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of the petition till the realization of the award amount.

The respondent No.2-Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order, thereafter recover the same from the respondent No.1 through due process of law.
The expenses to be incurred for future medication shall not carry any interest.

After deposit of the compensation amount with interest, 40% is directed to be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank in F.D for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.

8. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this court has framed the following issues;
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that, he had sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident,
that was taken place on 25-08-2019 at about 2-00 p.m. on Maddur - Malavalli Main road, near Kullappa Military Hotel, Bugathagahalli village, Malavalli Taluk,
Mandya due to the rash and negligent driving of the rider of the Pulsar Motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-02-JR-6295 in an actionable negligence?

from whom?
3) What order or award?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Upon investigation, the Investigation Officer of the case has filed charge sheet against the rider of the offending vehicle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 338 of IPC and Section 3 R/W Section 181 of IMV Act.
17. The respondent No.2, disputed the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-02-JR-6295, but not examined the rider of the offending vehicle or any of the independent witness who witnessed the alleged accident to prove the same.
Though the respondent No.2 examined Assistant Manager Legal(Claims) as RW1, but his evidence is only with regard to the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-02-JR-6295 had no valid and effective driving licence to ride the said vehicle as on the date of accident.
Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
"In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.
Hence, by taking into consideration of point of disability expressed by PW2, it is apt to take whole body disability as 9%
instead of 26%.
In this regard, there is no iota of documents to show his income per month.
In the absence of the material documents, notional income has to be taken into consideration.
But the said notional income is to be taken judiciously, by taking into consideration of the year of the accident.
As such, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
38. The respondent No.2 has contended that the rider of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
Thereby violated the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
To disprove the contents of the charge sheet and to show that,
the rider had valid D.L. no supportive evidence is available on record to impeach the recitals of Ex.P8.
Moreover, respondent No.1 being the owner and the rider of the motor cycle remained absent, placed exparte.
Hence, it is crystal clear that, there is a clear violation of the terms and conditions of the policy.
It is violation of terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
Hence, respondent No.1 is not liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and has relied the judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.6154/2019 between Hemalatha @ Hema @ Hemavathi & Others Vs. Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd., & Another and MFA 3297/2019 between Adilakshmamma & Others Vs.
Shri Raju B. & Another 41.
1). 2004 (3) SCC 297 between National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Swaran Singh & Others
Dasaratha.S vs Naveen.O on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84315759/
9 2) 2018 SCC 208 between Pappu & Others Vs. Vinod Kumar Lamba & Another
In the light of the discussion held above, I am of the view that, though the respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle, cannot escape from his liability to pay compensation to the petitioner, in view of violation of terms and conditions of the policy.
But, to protect the interest of the petitioner, it is necessary to direct the respondent No.2-insurance company to pay compensation to the petitioner and thereafter to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle, through due process of law.

O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for  compensation of Rs.4,92,564/- (Rupees  four lakh ninety two thousand five hundred and sixty four only) along with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of the petition till the realization of the award amount.
The respondent No.2-Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order, thereafter recover the same from the respondent No.1 through due process of law.
The expenses to be incurred for future medication shall not carry any interest.
After deposit of the compensation amount with interest, 40% is directed to be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank in F.D for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
